bank_access: SA FICA/AML KYC requires in-person branch verification; Standard Bank, Nedbank make the signatory appear. Non-residents give passport + foreign address proof; remote NPC/trust onboarding is effectively impossible.

Effectively blocked: Dutch banks (ING, ABN AMRO, Rabobank) apply strict Wwft AML screening; non-resident founders without a local address/BSN are routinely declined. In-person plus local presence is effectively required.

Non-resident accounts are legal, but a branch visit is required: in-person ID, enhanced AML due diligence, and many banks demand a Belgian address — non-resident business accounts are frequently refused.

No legal bar for non-residents, but a local visit is typical: strict AML banks apply enhanced due diligence to overseas founders; remote applications are often delayed or refused. A local mandate is the workaround.

Effectively blocked for remote non-residents: French banks demand proof of French address + in-person signature; AML refusals are common (droit au compte as remedy). Association accounts need a local visit/agent.

Some direct banks allow remote onboarding via video ID/eID, but most require in-person signature; non-residents face AML scrutiny and banks often demand a local address. A local representative is the practical route.

Branch visit required: Austrian banks do in-person KYC and most accounts need proof of Austrian residence (Meldezettel). Non-residents without local presence are refused; a local representative is needed.

Non-resident onboarding exists (some banks allow remote video), but Swiss AML/KYC is strict and domestic registration (representative/domicile) is required. A local representative is needed for a Stiftung/Verein.

Effectively blocked for small remote founders: Liechtenstein banks serve non-residents mainly via private banking with high minimum deposits, in-person meetings and strict AML. A local agent/mandate is required.

Effectively blocked for remote non-residents: Monaco banks demand high minimum deposits (EUR 500k+), a local address and in-person onboarding; non-EU non-residents face strictest thresholds. A local agent is required.

No general remote onboarding; non-residents must open accounts in person at branches (e.g. CAI) with passport + foreign address proof. Strict AML screening makes a local visit or representative required.
Non-residents can open accounts but a branch visit is typical; banks demand a local address, high non-resident minimum deposits (often EUR 250k+), and strict AML. A local agent is the common route.

Non-resident corporate accounts are possible, but most banks (PKO, mBank) require in-person signature and some a Polish address; enhanced AML checks on the UBO are common, so a local representative is practical.

No legal bar, but banks (Ceska sporitelna, Moneta) generally require in-person signature with passport + address proof; many refuse non-resident business accounts. A local visit or representative is needed.

Non-resident accounts are legal, but a branch visit is typical: banks demand a residence permit or proof of employment (esp. non-EU), in-person ID and often a local address. A local visit/representative is needed.

Effectively blocked for remote founders: Hungarian banks (OTP, KB) require in-person onboarding, and non-residents need proof of a Hungarian address/residence. Non-resident business accounts are rare; local agent needed.

Non-residents may open accounts (even tourists in principle), but a branch visit is typical: banks demand a Slovenian tax number, in-person ID verification and often a local address. A visit/representative is needed.

Non-resident business accounts are possible, but a personal branch visit is required (PBZ etc.), with enhanced AML checks and usually a Croatian OIB number. A local representative is needed for remote founders.

A local visit is typical: Bosnian banks require in-person onboarding with passport, and non-residents need a clear local connection; the system is fragmented (FBiH/SRH). A local agent/representative is the common route.

No remote onboarding: Serbian banks require an in-person visit with passport + foreign address proof; non-residents can open (incl. EUR) accounts at bank discretion — a local representative is needed.
